questions.stem: Why do esters have lower boiling points than carboxylic acids of similar molecular mass?

options.text: Esters cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other because the -OH group is no longer present
Esters are gases at room temperature

questions.explanation: In esterification, the -OH group of the acid is used up to form the ester link (-COO-). Without a free -OH group, ester molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other, only weaker van der Waals forces. This means less energy is needed to separate them, giving lower boiling points.
